graph-pool ceiling (precondition for #31 and any long-context staged serve): a staged stage caches ONE ggml graph per state-column WINDOW; stage 3 (20 layers) costs ~7.5 MiB of its 205.7 MB metadata pool per graph, so ~26 distinct windows per stage is the practical ceiling (~1700 tokens at cap 64); the session-1 pass-cap-1 collapse hit that ceiling at graph ~26. Raising the pool or evicting cold graphs is REQUIRED before a 4096+ staged serve
findings: 1. pass-cap collapse: a staged run with no --prefill-chunk took cap=min(relay, max(1,0))=1; at cap 1 every token gets its own column and its own cached graph, and stage 3's ggml pool died after ~26 graphs ('ggml_new_object: needed 205986800, available 205676800' - the pool's FULL size). Fixed in 9674c6d0 (staged takes the relay unit; prints a line). Default path untouched (relay_pass_cap only set when --gpus).

2. a repeated identical prompt (521x one sentence) made BOTH arms emit EOS as the first sampled token - the engine stops unconditionally at G.eos; long-prompt witnesses need non-degenerate text (the runner now numbers the repetitions and appends an elicitation tail).

3. witness #8's GLM PASS (2026-10-24 receipt) ran under the same admission confound (its control prefetched, its staged arm did not, no --slots on GLM); one staged run matched 64/64, which today's perfect control twin shows was knife-edge luck. The GLM parity protocol must equalize --pf-b (and ideally slots) on both sides.
